## Predictions: Independent Heads at Work {.smaller}

```{python}
#| label: load-predictions-naf-multilevel-slide

import json
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go

PRED_BUCKET_ML = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/predictions/naf_multilevel"
ARCH_FILES_ML  = {
    "FastText":                   "fasttext.npz",
    "FastText + Label Attention": "fasttext_labatt.npz",
}
LEVEL_NAMES     = ["sec", "div", "grp", "cls", "sub"]
LEVEL_LABELS_ML = {"sec": "Section", "div": "Division", "grp": "Group", "cls": "Class", "sub": "Sub-class"}
NAF_PARQUET_URL = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/datasets/naf_merged.parquet"

PREDS_DIR_ML = Path("results/naf_multilevel/preds")
PREDS_DIR_ML.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

preds_by_arch_ml = {}
for arch, fname in ARCH_FILES_ML.items():
    cache = PREDS_DIR_ML / fname
    try:
        if not cache.exists():
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{PRED_BUCKET_ML}/{fname}", cache)
        d = np.load(cache, allow_pickle=True)
        preds_by_arch_ml[arch] = {"y_test": d["y_test"].astype(int)}
        preds_by_arch_ml[arch].update({
            f"y_pred_{lvl}": d[f"y_pred_{lvl}"].astype(int) for lvl in LEVEL_NAMES
        })
    except Exception:
        pass

ARCHS_AVAIL_ML = list(preds_by_arch_ml.keys())

# Multi-level's per-level label encoders differ from single-level's — reconstruct
# them the same way naf_multilevel.qmd does (cached locally after the first run).
classes_cache = PREDS_DIR_ML / "level_classes.json"
if classes_cache.exists():
    LEVEL_CLASSES = json.loads(classes_cache.read_text())
else:
    df_full_ml = pd.read_parquet(NAF_PARQUET_URL, columns=["libelle_cleaned"] + LEVEL_NAMES).dropna()
    LEVEL_CLASSES = {lvl: sorted(df_full_ml[lvl].astype(str).unique().tolist()) for lvl in LEVEL_NAMES}
    classes_cache.write_text(json.dumps(LEVEL_CLASSES))

def code_of(level: str, idx: int) -> str:
    return LEVEL_CLASSES[level][idx]

# Reuses `_naf_struct`, `preds_by_arch`, `ARCHS_AVAIL`, `class_code` from the
# single-level Predictions slide earlier in this deck, for the truncated-cascade
# comparison — same underlying NAF structure, no need to refetch.
DIVISION_TO_SECTION_ML = {div: s["id"] for s in _naf_struct["sections"] for div in s["divisions"]}

SINGLE_LEVELS_ML = [
    ("Section",   lambda c: DIVISION_TO_SECTION_ML.get(c[:2], "?")),
    ("Division",  lambda c: c[:2]),
    ("Group",     lambda c: c[:3]),
    ("Class",     lambda c: c[:4]),
    ("Sub-class", lambda c: c),
]
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Hierarchical Accuracy

```{python}
#| label: fig-hierarchy-direct-naf-multilevel-slide
#| fig-cap: "Error rate by hierarchy level: multi-level's independent heads vs. single-level's truncated cascade"

level_acc_ml = {}
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL_ML:
    d = preds_by_arch_ml[arch]
    level_acc_ml[arch] = [
        (d[f"y_pred_{lvl}"] == d["y_test"][:, i]).mean() * 100
        for i, lvl in enumerate(LEVEL_NAMES)
    ]

error_single_ml = {}
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL:
    d = preds_by_arch[arch]
    true_codes = [class_code(c) for c in d["y_test"]]
    pred_codes = [class_code(c) for c in d["y_pred"]]
    error_single_ml[arch] = [
        100 - np.mean([fn(t) == fn(p) for t, p in zip(true_codes, pred_codes)]) * 100
        for _, fn in SINGLE_LEVELS_ML
    ]

x_lvls_ml = [LEVEL_LABELS_ML[l] for l in LEVEL_NAMES]

fig = go.Figure()
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL_ML:
    err_ml = [100 - a for a in level_acc_ml[arch]]
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=x_lvls_ml, y=err_ml, mode="lines+markers", name=f"{arch} — multi-level heads",
        line=dict(color=COLORS_ML.get(arch, "grey"), width=2.5), marker=dict(size=10),
        hovertemplate="%{x}<br>error rate=%{y:.1f}%<extra>" + arch + " — multi-level</extra>",
    ))
for arch, errs in error_single_ml.items():
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=x_lvls_ml, y=errs, mode="lines+markers", name=f"{arch} — single-level (truncated)",
        line=dict(color=COLORS_ML.get(arch, "grey"), width=2.5, dash="dot"),
        marker=dict(size=8, symbol="diamond"),
        hovertemplate="%{x}<br>error rate=%{y:.1f}%<extra>" + arch + " — single-level</extra>",
    ))

all_err_vals = [v for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL_ML for v in [100 - a for a in level_acc_ml[arch]]]
all_err_vals += [v for errs in error_single_ml.values() for v in errs]
y_pad = (max(all_err_vals) - min(all_err_vals)) * 0.1

fig.update_layout(
    template="simple_white",
    xaxis_title="Hierarchy level", yaxis_title="Error rate (%)",
    yaxis=dict(range=[min(all_err_vals) - y_pad, max(all_err_vals) + y_pad]),
    legend_title="Architecture — approach", height=400, width=820,
)
fig.show()
```

- Counter-intuitive: dedicated independent heads were expected to clearly beat truncation at the coarser levels — instead they stay close, tying at Sub-class

### Hierarchical Accuracy — v2

```{python}
#| label: fig-hierarchy-errors-naf-multilevel-slide
#| fig-cap: "Among wrong sub-class predictions, the finest level that still lands correctly — multi-level's independent heads vs. single-level's truncated cascade"

BUCKET_ORDER_ML  = ["cls", "grp", "div", "sec"]
BUCKET_LABELS_ML = {"cls": "Class", "grp": "Group", "div": "Division", "sec": "Section"}
ERROR_BUCKETS_ML = ["Class", "Group", "Division", "Section", "No match"]
BUCKET_COLORS_ML = {
    "Class":      "#66BB6A",
    "Group":      "#FFCA28",
    "Division":   "#FB8C00",
    "Section":    "#E53935",
    "No match":   "#7B0000",
}

error_shares_ml = {}
overall_acc_ml  = {}
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL_ML:
    d = preds_by_arch_ml[arch]
    y_test = d["y_test"]
    correct = {lvl: (d[f"y_pred_{lvl}"] == y_test[:, i]) for i, lvl in enumerate(LEVEL_NAMES)}
    overall_acc_ml[arch] = correct["sub"].mean() * 100

    wrong_idx = np.where(~correct["sub"])[0]
    assigned  = np.full(len(wrong_idx), "No match", dtype=object)
    remaining = np.ones(len(wrong_idx), dtype=bool)
    for lvl in BUCKET_ORDER_ML:
        is_correct_here = correct[lvl][wrong_idx] & remaining
        assigned[is_correct_here] = BUCKET_LABELS_ML[lvl]
        remaining &= ~is_correct_here

    counts = pd.Series(assigned).value_counts()
    error_shares_ml[arch] = {b: counts.get(b, 0) / len(wrong_idx) * 100 for b in ERROR_BUCKETS_ML}

SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY_ML = {name: fn for name, fn in SINGLE_LEVELS_ML}
SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY_ML = {
    "sec": SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY_ML["Section"],
    "div": SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY_ML["Division"],
    "grp": SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY_ML["Group"],
    "cls": SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY_ML["Class"],
}

error_shares_single_ml = {}
overall_acc_single_ml  = {}
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL:
    d = preds_by_arch[arch]
    true_codes  = np.array([class_code(c) for c in d["y_test"]])
    pred_codes  = np.array([class_code(c) for c in d["y_pred"]])
    correct_sub = true_codes == pred_codes
    overall_acc_single_ml[arch] = correct_sub.mean() * 100

    wrong_idx = np.where(~correct_sub)[0]
    t_wrong, p_wrong = true_codes[wrong_idx], pred_codes[wrong_idx]
    assigned  = np.full(len(wrong_idx), "No match", dtype=object)
    remaining = np.ones(len(wrong_idx), dtype=bool)
    for lvl in BUCKET_ORDER_ML:
        fn = SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY_ML[lvl]
        is_correct_here = (np.array([fn(t) for t in t_wrong]) == np.array([fn(p) for p in p_wrong])) & remaining
        assigned[is_correct_here] = BUCKET_LABELS_ML[lvl]
        remaining &= ~is_correct_here

    counts = pd.Series(assigned).value_counts()
    error_shares_single_ml[arch] = {b: counts.get(b, 0) / len(wrong_idx) * 100 for b in ERROR_BUCKETS_ML}

bar_order_ml = []
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL_ML:
    bar_order_ml.append(("ml", arch))
    if arch in preds_by_arch:
        bar_order_ml.append(("single", arch))

x_labels_combined_ml = [
    f"{arch}<br>multi-level<i> ({100 - overall_acc_ml[arch]:.1f}% wrong)</i>" if kind == "ml"
    else f"{arch}<br>single-level<i> ({100 - overall_acc_single_ml[arch]:.1f}% wrong)</i>"
    for kind, arch in bar_order_ml
]
patterns_combined_ml = ["" if kind == "ml" else "/" for kind, arch in bar_order_ml]

fig = go.Figure()
for bucket in ERROR_BUCKETS_ML:
    vals = [
        error_shares_ml[arch][bucket] if kind == "ml" else error_shares_single_ml[arch][bucket]
        for kind, arch in bar_order_ml
    ]
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
        x=x_labels_combined_ml, y=vals, name=bucket,
        marker=dict(color=BUCKET_COLORS_ML[bucket], pattern=dict(shape=patterns_combined_ml)),
        text=[f"{v:.1f}%" for v in vals],
        textposition="inside", insidetextfont=dict(color="white", size=11),
        hovertemplate="%{x}<br>" + bucket + ": %{y:.1f}% of errors<extra></extra>",
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    template="simple_white", barmode="stack",
    xaxis_title=None, yaxis_title="Share of wrong sub-class predictions (%)",
    yaxis=dict(range=[0, 100]),
    legend_title="Finest level<br>that still lands right", height=420, width=820,
)
fig.show()
```

- "No match" (missing even the section) drops from ~47–48% under single-level's truncated cascade to **34.0%** (FastText) / **28.9%** (Label Attention) once each level gets its own head

### Independent Heads Effect

```{python}
#| label: fig-hierarchy-independence-naf-multilevel-slide
#| fig-cap: "Section/division accuracy among wrong sub-class predictions: truncating the wrong guess vs. asking the independent head directly"

from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

GAP_LEVELS_ML = ["sec", "div"]
GAP_LABELS_ML = {"sec": "Section", "div": "Division"}
TRUNC_FNS_ML  = {
    "sec": lambda c: DIVISION_TO_SECTION_ML.get(c[:2], "?"),
    "div": lambda c: c[:2],
}

fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=len(ARCHS_AVAIL_ML), subplot_titles=ARCHS_AVAIL_ML,
                    horizontal_spacing=0.12)

for col, arch in enumerate(ARCHS_AVAIL_ML, start=1):
    d = preds_by_arch_ml[arch]
    y_test = d["y_test"]
    wrong_sub = d["y_pred_sub"] != y_test[:, 4]
    pred_sub_codes = np.array([code_of("sub", c) for c in d["y_pred_sub"][wrong_sub]])

    trunc_accs, direct_accs = [], []
    for i, lvl in enumerate(GAP_LEVELS_ML):
        true_codes  = np.array([code_of(lvl, c) for c in y_test[wrong_sub, i]])
        trunc_codes = np.array([TRUNC_FNS_ML[lvl](c) for c in pred_sub_codes])
        trunc_accs.append((trunc_codes == true_codes).mean() * 100)
        direct_accs.append((d[f"y_pred_{lvl}"][wrong_sub] == y_test[wrong_sub, i]).mean() * 100)

    x_labels = [GAP_LABELS_ML[l] for l in GAP_LEVELS_ML]
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
        x=x_labels, y=trunc_accs, name="Truncated (from the wrong sub-class guess)",
        legendgroup="trunc", showlegend=(col == 1),
        marker=dict(color="#bbbbbb", pattern_shape="/"),
        text=[f"{v:.1f}%" for v in trunc_accs], textposition="outside",
        hovertemplate="%{x}<br>truncated: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
    ), row=1, col=col)
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
        x=x_labels, y=direct_accs, name="Direct (independent head)",
        legendgroup="direct", showlegend=(col == 1),
        marker=dict(color=COLORS_ML.get(arch, "grey")),
        text=[f"{v:.1f}%" for v in direct_accs], textposition="outside",
        hovertemplate="%{x}<br>direct: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
    ), row=1, col=col)
    fig.update_yaxes(range=[0, 75], title_text="Accuracy (%)" if col == 1 else "", row=1, col=col)

fig.update_layout(
    barmode="group", template="simple_white", height=400,
    legend=dict(orientation="h", x=0.5, xanchor="center", y=-0.22, yanchor="top"),
    margin=dict(t=40, b=90),
)
fig.show()
```

- Restricted to the model's own wrong sub-class guesses: asking the independent head directly beats truncating that same wrong guess by **+8.6pp** at Section / **+9.6pp** at Division for FastText, **+9.9pp** / **+13.1pp** for Label Attention

:::

## Taking It Further {.smaller}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Independent Heads Don't Agree

- The previous slide is a real win: asking a head directly beats truncating a wrong sub-class guess by up to **+13pp**, and mistakes stay **localised to one head**
- But that's an *aggregate* statistic. For any single description, nothing forces the 5 heads to **agree with each other** — the section head can predict "C" while the sub-class head's own true parent is "A"
- The joint loss ℒ = ℒ<sub>sec</sub> + ℒ<sub>div</sub> + ℒ<sub>grp</sub> + ℒ<sub>cls</sub> + ℒ<sub>sub</sub> only compares each head to **its own** ground truth — it never compares heads **to each other**, so disagreement is never penalized
- 5 independent guesses that can contradict each other aren't a single coherent hierarchical code — the ambiguity didn't disappear, it just **moved downstream**
- Even with the loss "harmonized" (summed, shared trunk), the heads don't really *communicate* — or not enough. Three ways to fix that:

### Consistency Loss

```{=html}
<div style="display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:18px;margin:16px 0;font-family:-apple-system,'Segoe UI',sans-serif;">
  <div style="background:#e8edf8;border:1.5px solid #1565C0;border-radius:9px;padding:10px 16px;text-align:center;">
    <div style="font-size:9px;color:#1565C0;font-weight:700;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.05em;">Section head</div>
    <div style="font-size:15px;font-weight:700;color:#0d47a1;margin-top:4px;">predicts "C"</div>
  </div>
  <div style="display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;">
    <div style="font-size:20px;color:#c62828;">⇹</div>
    <div style="font-size:9px;color:#c62828;font-weight:700;white-space:nowrap;">inconsistent</div>
  </div>
  <div style="background:#dce8f5;border:1.5px solid #1e88e5;border-radius:9px;padding:10px 16px;text-align:center;">
    <div style="font-size:9px;color:#1e88e5;font-weight:700;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.05em;">Sub-class head</div>
    <div style="font-size:15px;font-weight:700;color:#0d47a1;margin-top:4px;">predicts "6201Y"</div>
    <div style="font-size:8.5px;color:#888;margin-top:2px;">(true section of 6201Y is "A")</div>
  </div>
</div>
<div style="text-align:center;font-size:11px;color:#ad1457;background:#fce4ec;border:1.5px dashed #e91e63;border-radius:8px;padding:6px 14px;max-width:440px;margin:0 auto;">
  New term: &Lscr;<sub>cons</sub> &mdash; penalize exactly this kind of disagreement
</div>
```

- **Idea**: add a term ℒ<sub>cons</sub> that fires whenever a finer head's prediction implies a coarser-level answer that disagrees with that coarser head's own prediction
- **Advantages**
  - Minimal change: same 5 independent heads, same inference cost, nothing added to the architecture
  - Directly targets the actual failure mode (agreement) instead of hoping accuracy alone fixes it
- **Disadvantages**
  - Only a *soft* constraint — encourages agreement statistically, doesn't guarantee it at inference

### Cascaded Heads

```{=html}
<div style="display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:4px;margin:16px 0;font-family:-apple-system,'Segoe UI',sans-serif;flex-wrap:nowrap;">
  <div style="background:#e8edf8;border:1.5px solid #0D3B77;border-radius:8px;padding:8px 10px;text-align:center;min-width:64px;">
    <div style="font-size:8px;color:#0D3B77;font-weight:700;text-transform:uppercase;">Section</div>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size:14px;color:#aaa;">→</div>
  <div style="background:#e0e9f7;border:1.5px solid #1565C0;border-radius:8px;padding:8px 10px;text-align:center;min-width:64px;">
    <div style="font-size:8px;color:#1565C0;font-weight:700;text-transform:uppercase;">Division</div>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size:14px;color:#aaa;">→</div>
  <div style="background:#d8e6f6;border:1.5px solid #1976D2;border-radius:8px;padding:8px 10px;text-align:center;min-width:64px;">
    <div style="font-size:8px;color:#1976D2;font-weight:700;text-transform:uppercase;">Group</div>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size:14px;color:#aaa;">→</div>
  <div style="background:#cfe0fb;border:1.5px solid #2196F3;border-radius:8px;padding:8px 10px;text-align:center;min-width:64px;">
    <div style="font-size:8px;color:#2196F3;font-weight:700;text-transform:uppercase;">Class</div>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size:14px;color:#aaa;">→</div>
  <div style="background:#c5dafa;border:1.5px solid #42A5F5;border-radius:8px;padding:8px 10px;text-align:center;min-width:64px;">
    <div style="font-size:8px;color:#2b8fe0;font-weight:700;text-transform:uppercase;">Sub-class</div>
  </div>
</div>
<div style="text-align:center;font-size:9.5px;color:#999;">each arrow = that head's embedding, concatenated into the next head's input</div>
```

- **Idea**: stop feeding all 5 heads the same shared trunk output in parallel. Instead, chain them — the section head's embedding (taken right before its own final linear layer) is concatenated into the division head's input, and so on down to sub-class
- **Advantages**
  - Consistency **by construction**: each head literally conditions on the coarser levels' representations, not just a shared trunk
  - Mirrors how a human coder actually works — section first, then narrow down
- **Disadvantages**
  - Purely sequential: 5 heads deep, so they can no longer be computed in parallel — slower to train **and** to run at inference
  - Errors now **propagate forward** — a wrong section early in the chain can drag every downstream head down with it

### Cross-Level Interaction

```{=html}
<div style="display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;gap:6px;margin:16px 0;font-family:-apple-system,'Segoe UI',sans-serif;">
  <div style="display:flex;gap:6px;">
    <div style="background:#e8edf8;border:1.5px solid #0D3B77;border-radius:7px;padding:6px 9px;font-size:8px;font-weight:700;color:#0D3B77;">Section</div>
    <div style="background:#e0e9f7;border:1.5px solid #1565C0;border-radius:7px;padding:6px 9px;font-size:8px;font-weight:700;color:#1565C0;">Division</div>
    <div style="background:#d8e6f6;border:1.5px solid #1976D2;border-radius:7px;padding:6px 9px;font-size:8px;font-weight:700;color:#1976D2;">Group</div>
    <div style="background:#cfe0fb;border:1.5px solid #2196F3;border-radius:7px;padding:6px 9px;font-size:8px;font-weight:700;color:#2196F3;">Class</div>
    <div style="background:#c5dafa;border:1.5px solid #42A5F5;border-radius:7px;padding:6px 9px;font-size:8px;font-weight:700;color:#2b8fe0;">Sub-class</div>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size:13px;color:#aaa;">⇕ ⇕ ⇕ ⇕ ⇕</div>
  <div style="background:#e8f5e9;border:1.5px solid #388e3c;border-radius:8px;padding:8px 20px;font-size:9px;font-weight:700;color:#1b5e20;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.05em;">
    &Sigma;&divide;n &mdash; average of the 5 level embeddings (shown here)
  </div>
  <div style="font-size:9px;color:#aaa;font-style:italic;">also possible: weighted average &middot; learned attention</div>
  <div style="font-size:13px;color:#aaa;">↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓</div>
  <div style="font-size:9px;color:#888;">5 enriched embeddings → 5 final linear heads</div>
</div>
```

- **Idea**: keep the 5 per-level embeddings, but before the final linear layers, let them **interact** — combine each level's embedding with the other 4 before its own head reads it. Simplest version, illustrated above: a plain **average** across the 5 embeddings; a **weighted average** or a learned **attention** block are fancier versions of the same idea
- **Advantages**
  - **Bidirectional** communication, unlike the cascade — a fine-level signal can inform a coarse prediction too, not just the reverse
  - Still one parallel pass over all 5 levels, not a 5-deep sequential chain
- **Disadvantages**
  - Still a *soft* form of consistency, not a guarantee — same limitation as the loss-based fix

:::

# Conclusion
